# Change object color

- Route: `/tools/change-image-color`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `photo`
- Slug: `change-image-color`

## Summary

Pick the color with an eyedropper, set how far the selection reaches, rotate the hue, and export: a red car becomes green with its shading and reflections intact. (Photo editing)

## Details

This page opens Aperture, the Media Manipulator photo editor, on the Color (HSL) panel with a Color range mask one click away, which is the pair of tools that recolors an object. The mask does the selecting: you click the object with the eyedropper, and every pixel is scored by how far its color is from the one you picked, measured in CIE Lab, with a Fuzziness slider setting the reach. The Color (HSL) layer does the changing: a hue rotation inside that mask turns the object a different color while its lightness and saturation, and therefore its shading, reflections and texture, stay as they were. The two are separate layers in the stack, so you can refine the selection after choosing the color and undo either one.
### What it does
- A Color range mask component selects pixels by their distance from a target color you pick in the photo; shift-click adds up to 8 targets so a car with two shades of red is one selection.
- Fuzziness from 0 to 100 sets the radius of the selection in Lab units, up to 60 at full fuzziness, with a soft edge in the outer half of that radius so the boundary of the object does not cut.
- A hue rotation on the Color (HSL) layer, master or per range, moves the selected pixels around the color wheel while HSL saturation and lightness are left exactly as they were.
- Mask components combine: intersect the color selection with a Radial, Linear gradient or Brush component to limit it to one object when the same color appears elsewhere in the frame; Invert flips it; Mask feather softens it.
- The mask can be viewed as an overlay or on its own, the layer keeps its own opacity and blend mode, and the export renders the original at full resolution with the same mask math.
### How to use it
1. Drop the photo: Any JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC, AVIF or TIFF. The editor opens with Color (HSL) in front and an empty mask ready on that layer.
2. Pick the color: In the Masks panel add a Color range component, click the object with the eyedropper, and raise Fuzziness until the whole object is covered in the mask overlay.
3. Rotate the hue: Move the All colors Hue slider until the object is the color you want; only the masked pixels change.
4. Refine and export: Add a Brush or Radial component with Intersect if the color appears elsewhere, feather the mask, then export JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or TIFF.
### Supported formats
- Input: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, TIFF, BMP
- Output: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF
- The Lab conversion and the mask blur run on every pixel of the original at export; a 20 megapixel file is rendered in a few seconds on the server.
- Transparent PNG originals keep their alpha: the mask and the color change never touch the alpha channel.
### Technical details
- The Color range mask converts both the pixel and each target to CIE Lab (D65, from linear sRGB) and takes the Euclidean distance dE between them, the 1976 delta E. The radius is R = Fuzziness / 100 x 60, and the mask value is 1 - smoothstep(0.5 R, R, dE): fully selected up to half the radius, a smooth falloff to zero at the full radius, and the largest value over all targets wins. A Fuzziness of 40 gives R = 24, so a pixel at dE 12 or less is fully selected and one at dE 24 or more is not selected at all.
- Components fold left to right: Add takes the maximum, Subtract takes min(m, 1 - component), Intersect takes the minimum. The folded mask is then blurred by a Gaussian with sigma = Mask feather / 100 x 0.05 x the long side of the photo, optionally inverted, and multiplied by Mask strength. The layer output per pixel is lerp(input, adjusted, m).
- The color change itself is the Color (HSL) formula: hue h + master Hue + the weighted range Hues, saturation and lightness untouched when their sliders are at 0, converted back to RGB. Because the mask is applied after the adjustment, a pixel at mask value 0.9 gets 90 percent of the way from its original to its recolored value, which is what makes edges blend.
- Lab distance includes lightness, so a deep shadow on a red object can be further from the picked red than a brick wall is. Pick two or three targets across the shading of the object with shift-click rather than raising Fuzziness until the wall comes along.
- What you see is a WebGL2 render on your GPU of a 1920 px copy; what you download is rendered on our server from the full-size original with identical Lab, smoothstep and HSL code, and matches within the documented tolerance, a mean of 1 and a maximum of 4 levels in 8 bits for color operations.
### When not to use it
A color selection cannot separate two objects of the same color in the same light; that is a job for a Brush or Radial mask, or for Select subject when the object is the main subject of the frame. It cannot create a color that is not a hue, so white, black and metallic finishes need a saturation and lightness change rather than a rotation, and it cannot change the pattern or material of a surface. When the whole photo has a cast rather than one object, use the white balance or color balance pages instead, and when you want the object cut out on a transparent background use the background remover.
### Use cases
- Product color variants: Shoot one colorway, pick it, and produce the rest by rotating the hue; the stitching and shadows are the same in every variant.
- Car and bike listings: Show the vehicle in the color a buyer asks about; two targets, one on the bright panel and one in the shadow, cover the whole body.
- Clothing in portraits: Change a shirt from yellow to blue; intersect the color selection with a Brush component so a yellow sign in the background is left alone.
- Walls and rooms: Try paint colors on a photo of the room; the color selection catches the wall and leaves the white trim because the trim is too far in Lab.
### FAQ
Q: How do I change the color of just one object when the same color appears twice?
A: Add a second mask component, a Radial or a Brush, drawn over the object you want, and set it to Intersect. The mask is then the minimum of the color selection and the shape, so the other object, which lies outside the shape, is left at zero.
Q: What does the Fuzziness slider actually control?
A: The Lab radius of the selection: Fuzziness divided by 100 times 60. Pixels closer than half that radius to a picked color are fully selected, pixels beyond it are not selected, and between the two the value falls along a smoothstep curve.
Q: Can I turn a red object white or black?
A: A hue rotation cannot, because white and black have no hue. Keep the same mask, set the Saturation slider to -100 on the Color (HSL) layer, and then use Lightness or a masked Curves layer to push the gray toward white or black.
Q: Why are the darkest parts of the object not selected?
A: Lab distance includes lightness, so the shadow side of a red car can be further from the color you clicked than a different object is. Shift-click a second target in the shadow instead of raising Fuzziness for everything.
Q: Does recoloring an object cost an AI operation?
A: No. The Color range mask and the hue rotation are ordinary adjustments computed from the pixels. Only Select subject and Heal use the AI models; a color selection is free, and the export counts as one everyday operation.
Q: Will the new color have the same shading as the old one?
A: Yes. The rotation changes only the hue angle; the HSL saturation and lightness of every pixel are preserved, so highlights, reflections and shadows keep their shape. Perceived brightness does shift between hues, which the live histogram will show.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Use when someone wants to recolour a specific object, like turning a red car green, by picking its colour with an eyedropper, setting fuzziness, and rotating the hue while shading stays intact.
When to send them elsewhere: It rotates hue only, so not for making something white, black or metallic, or changing material. A whole-photo cast belongs in White balance (white-balance-photo). To cut the object out onto transparency use Remove Background from Image (remove-background-from-image).
Related tools: adjust-image-hue (shift hues across the whole photo); select-by-color (build a colour-range mask); color-pop (keep one colour, grey the rest); remove-background-from-image (cut the object out)
